title: You can't just vibe code a game
author: xaeru
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/7zhkoo53tk3i1.png

I’ve been building a 3D game with AI assistance, and I’m honestly feeling defeated looking at my progress. It made me realize that **you truly can't just vibe code a game.** People actually shipping good-looking games with AI are not vibe coding.

comments.author: Dorkin_Aint_Easy
comments.body:
It is indeed very hard still even with AI. The expectation is that if you want a highly dynamic game that has a good story line you’ll be building it for years. It’s a slow process but when I get stuck or feel defeated I tend to go back to brain storming with Claude and learn there is a better path or route that will accomplish the stuck task. 

My game is far from done but it’s light years ahead of where I started. I’ve probably reiterated it a hundred times. And there will be hundreds more.

comments.author: CraftyXII
comments.body:
Im finding if you hand it assets blue prints and examples it does a lot better that just build me this.   

Humble is great for tons of asset variety for cheap.

But even with that it cant replace humans long term vision for a final product it just helps you in getting there.

And it has to be built in small modules vs all at once.

Break it down into smaller subsystems that u can later tie together not doing this will lead to a bunch of half built systems that it says are done and ready to ship that are not even wired up.

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body: You don’t need to become an artist, you need to become an art director. This means having Claude or whatever AI you use teach you just enough about modeling, texturing, lighting, and rendering so you can direct it towards good results. It’s easy to one shot better results than you are getting if you work from concept art and real world reference images, set visual targets, settle on the various techniques that will be used like layer textures with shaders, lighting, polygon counts, etc. It also helps to have an existing library of high quality PBR materials for the agent to work with and if you don’t yet know what a PBR material is well that’s your next step. All you have to do is be curious and keeping going.

comments.author: poojer_hoojer

Game design is hard and takes a long time, and you can't rely on the AI to do it for you because the AI lacks taste.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
you can. you just aren't doing it right.

AIs will default to simply 3d geometry if you aren't specifying a style. It is just what it does.

if you want to go with a top-down approach i.e. get a functional game first, then refine the game

you still need to plan it out i.e. how are the assets getting replaced with better ones

your project will probably look better if you simply provide some visual references 

even better if you use dedicated 3d tools or have custom skills etc

iterating is more than just "keep prompting until it is better". there are some planning and preparation involved

vibe coding without planning and preparation will not give you anything impressive by default 

just keep trying and keep learning what AIs can do well etc.

comments.author: Vegetable_Voice_2044
comments.body:
I'm a bit obsessive about the organization of my project files. I try to keep everything component based so features don't share the same script or resources. Everything plugs into something like a content tree.
I cannot write any code myself so it's all vibe codes, and I don't bother to read even a single line of it. I just test the results and applaud or complain to Claude.

With 30 years of gaming experience I know what j want, and have seen many implementations of the features im trying to include in my project.

Between the focus on compartmentalization and organization, and the experience of 30 years of gaming. I believe I can vibe code a game. No YouTube tutorials telling me how to organize my stuff, or any of that tutorial hell nonsense... Just a lot, and I mean A LOT of back and forth discussion with the ai about what I want, and how exactly it should work. Helps if you reference existing features you wish to imitate.

Edit: your before and after changes having grass? I don't get it...

I mean look up the literal definition of vibe coding, it’s a term coined by Karpathy. Vibe Coding by definition is letting the AI handle the code while you handle the direction.
